question.worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{-3|x|+2} & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{3x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}{e}^{3x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3x+2}\,{|}_{a}^{0}\,) \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3a+2}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand ${e}^{-3|x|+2}$ is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2}}{3}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-3|x|+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{3} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{2}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
